parts.summary: Created scripts/core.py: a pure-Python (no ROS, no numpy) module porting the legacy MIT rrt_exploration functions.py to Python3. Exposes index_of_point, point_of_index, informationGain, discount, gridValue, pathCost, and the new select_goal. Preserves original Python2 integer-division semantics via //, adds safety bounds (gridValue returns 100 out-of-bounds, invalid resolution guards, no negative indexing), and select_goal implements information-gain-minus-travel-cost scoring with hysteresis, deterministic tie handling, and occupied/frontier filtering.

Migrated the ROS1 global_rrt_detector.cpp + functions.cpp to a single ROS2 Jazzy rrt_detector.cpp. Preserves the full RRT algorithm (random sampling, Nearest, Steer, ObstacleFree with free/unknown/obstacle classification), uses bounded timer callbacks (no blocking loops), subscribes to /map with transient_local QoS, publishes /detected_points as PointStamped with map-header frame id (leading-slash normalized). Adds fallback initialization from map bounds + TF robot position (or map center) when /clicked_point points are not received. Declares eta, map_topic, points_topic, robot_frame, global_frame, max_goals, random_seed, use_sim_time parameters. Includes bounds-checked gridValue (returns 100 out-of-bounds/invalid), zero-resolution validation, and std::mt19937 seeded RNG. Includes MIT attribution.

Migrated scripts/filter.py from ROS1 rrt_exploration to ROS2 Jazzy. Key changes: rospy→rclpy with bounded timer callback (no blocking loops); sklearn.MeanShift replaced with a numpy-only mean-shift implementation; `from functions import ...` → `import core`; tf.TransformListener → tf2_ros Buffer/TransformListener with bounded timeout Duration; frame IDs normalized (leading slash stripped); transient-local QoS for /map subscription; use_sim_time declared; graceful handling of missing map/TF/costmap (early returns, throttled warnings, fallback to map for clearing check); shutdown flag cancels timer and stops dispatch. Preserves original algorithm: accumulate detected points in map frame, mean-shift cluster (bandwidth 0.3), clear frontiers where gridValue>threshold OR informationGain<0.2, publish filtered centroids as PointArray plus visualization markers. MIT attribution retained.

Migrated the ROS1 rrrt_exploration assigner to ROS2 Jazzy as scripts/assigner.py. The node subscribes to /map (transient-local QoS) and /filtered_points (goose_rrt_exploration/PointArray), looks up TF map->base_link with bounded timeouts, and drives a single async Nav2 NavigateToPose goal. It uses core.informationGain, core.discount, and core.gridValue to compute information-gain-minus-travel-cost revenue with hysteresis (matching the legacy algorithm), skips occupied/out-of-map candidates (gridValue >= 50), and selects the maximum-scoring frontier with deterministic first-max tie handling. Goal orientation.w=1.0 and frame_id is taken from the /map header with leading slash removed. A timer callback (bounded, no blocking) dispatches goals only when idle and within max_goals/delay limits. The node publishes /goose/exploration_status (std_msgs/String JSON) with completed_goals, failed_goals, selected_goal, state, and position. On shutdown it cancels the active goal and stops dispatching. Configurable parameters: map_topic, frontiers_topic, info_radius, info_multiplier, hysteresis_radius, hysteresis_gain, global_frame, robot_frame, max_goals, random_seed, delay_after_assignment, rate, action_server. Includes MIT attribution. Python3 shebang, imports core from beside the script.

Package-level files for goose_rrt_exploration ROS2 Jazzy migration: CMakeLists.txt (ament_cmake + rosidl_default_generators, builds rrt_detector, installs Python scripts with core.py beside them, installs launch), package.xml (format 3, ament_cmake buildtool, geometry_msgs/nav_msgs/tf2 deps, rosidl interface group), msg/PointArray.msg (geometry_msgs/Point[] points), launch/exploration.launch.py (rrt_detector + filter.py + assigner.py nodes with configurable map/points/frontiers topics, frames, max_goals, random_seed, use_sim_time=true), and README.md with original MIT attribution.
